form.idDescription: The task ID is used to run the task using the command line tool or via the API. It must be unique and contain only alphanumeric characters and dashes. By default, it is generated from the task name.
form.name: Task name
form.nameDescription: The name of the task is used to identify the task in the dashboard.
form.scheduleDescription: Use the cron format to define the schedule of the task. We will ensure that the task runs as specified, and an incident will be created if the task is late or does not run.
form.isScheduledTaskDescription: Check this box if this is a recurring task. We will ensure that the task runs as specified, and an incident will be created if the task is late or does not run.
form.startWindowDescription: The start window is the time window during which the task is expected to run. If the task does not start in this window, it will be considered late and an incident will be created.
form.latenessWindowDescription: The lateness window is the time window, beginning after the start window, during which a late task is still expected to run. If the late task does not start in this window, it will be considered failed.
form.metadataDescription: Metadata is optional. It allows you to organize your tasks and related incidents.
form.heartbeatTimeoutDescription: Once a task is started, it is expected to send a periodic heartbeat to DutyDuck to confirm it is still running. If the task does not send a heartbeat in this window, it will be considered dead and an incident will be created. If you use the DutyDuck command line tool to start the task, the heartbeat is sent automatically.
form.taskIdNotAvailable: Task id is not available, a task with this id already exists.
form.notificationSettingsDescription: Determines the notifications that will be sent in case of task failure
form.scheduleTimezoneDescription: Time zone used to compute the scheduled execution time for the task
